deep.reconstruction:
SETTING (my interpretation). There are six unknowns x,y,z,ξ,η,ζ, numbered 1,3,5,2,4,6 as on the page, and four linear forms (1):
R0 = x+y+z+ξ+η+ζ,
R1 = αx+βy+γz+ξ/α+η/β+ζ/γ,
R2 (one prime), R3 (two primes).
So the coefficient columns are 1:(1,α,α',α''), 2:(1,1/α,1/α',1/α''), 3:(1,β,…), 4:(1,1/β,…), 5:(1,γ,…), 6:(1,1/γ,…).

The swap α↔1/α (likewise for β and γ) exchanges columns 1↔2, 3↔4, 5↔6. It is a symmetry of the whole system.

(2) Riemann assumes the four forms are linearly dependent, with multipliers (1,λ,λ',λ''). Column by column this gives six scalar equations:
- 1+αλ+α'λ'+α''λ''=0,
- 1+λ/α+λ'/α'+λ''/α''=0,
- the same two with β and with γ.
The page writes only the first and '…'. The problem is therefore: find the conditions on the 9 parameters for the 4×6 matrix to have rank ≤3, and express them through minors.

(3) Move the double-primed terms to the right in the two α-equations and multiply them: (1+αλ+α'λ')(1+λ/α+λ'/α') = (−α''λ'')(−λ''/α'') = λ''².

(4) Expand (3):
1 + (α+1/α)λ + (α'+1/α')λ' + (α/α'+α'/α)λλ' + λ²+λ'² = λ''².
The same holds with β and with γ. The terms 1, λ², λ'², λ''² are common, so the remaining λ-dependent parts must agree for α, β and γ.

(5) Use (2) again, in the forms αλ+α'λ' = −1−α''λ'' and λ/α+λ'/α' = −1−λ''/α'', inside the expansion of (3). This gives:
1 + (α''+1/α'')λ'' = (α'/α+α/α')λλ' + λ²+λ'² − λ''².

(6) Subtract the β-version of (5) from the α-version:
(α''+1/α''−β''−1/β'')λ'' = (α'/α+α/α'−β'/β−β/β')λλ'.
The same holds with γ in place of β.

MINORS. (ijk) denotes the 3×3 minor of rows R0,R1,R2 in columns i,j,k. Since R0 has all entries 1, it equals (b−a)(c'−a')−(c−a)(b'−a').
- (136) = (1/γ−α)(α'−β') + (1/γ'−α')(β−α).
- (154) = (1/β−α)(α'−γ') + (1/β'−α')(γ−α).
The '(αβγ')/(αγβ')' at the end of that line is most likely the column-notation (α β 1/γ)/(α γ 1/β), i.e. the same ratio.

Dependence of the rows means the minors over rows (0,1,3), (0,2,3), (1,2,3) are proportional to those over (0,1,2). The proportionality factor does not depend on the column triple. So the ratio (136)/(154) can be computed from any row triple. This is why Riemann writes the same ratio with the double primes, citing '(2)'.

(7) Take the combination (1/α)M013 − (1/α')M023 in both numerator and denominator (my reconstruction of how it arises). It gives
(136)/(154) = [A a + B b]/[C c + D d], with:
- A = 1/(αγ)−1/(α'γ'), a = α''−β'', B = 1/γ''−α'', b = β/α−β'/α';
- C = 1/(αβ)−1/(α'β'), c = α''−γ'', D = 1/β''−α'', d = γ/α−γ'/α'.

From (6). Use αα'·C·b = α'/α+α/α'−β'/β−β/β' and α''+1/α''−β''−1/β'' = −(α''−β'')(1/β''−α'')/α''. Together with the γ-analogue, (6) gives
a·D/(c·B) = C·b/(A·d), i.e. Aa·Dd = Bb·Cc.

Mediant step. From Aa/Cc = Bb/Dd and (7) it follows that Aa/Cc = Bb/Dd = (136)/(154). This is the next displayed line, 'aus (6) und (7)'.

Dual line. Apply the symmetry α↔1/α etc.:
(αγ−α'γ')/(αβ−α'β') · (1/α''−1/β'')/(1/α''−1/γ'') = (245)/(263) = (γ''−1/α'')(α/β−α'/β')/((β''−1/α'')(α/γ−α'/γ')).

Divide the two first members. All factors cancel except ββ'β''/(γγ'γ''). Hence
ββ'β''/(γγ'γ'') = (136)(263)/((154)(245)) = (136)(236)/((254)(154)),
the two sign changes from transposing columns cancelling. Applying the swap γ↔1/γ (columns 5↔6) gives
ββ'β''γγ'γ'' = (135)(235)/((264)(164)).

The two scribbled lines are partial expansions of the minors, with sign slips.

Last line. Here (α 1/β γ) etc. are minors labelled by column entries: (α 1/β γ)=(145), (α 1/β 1/γ)=(146), (1/α β γ)=(235), (1/α β 1/γ)=(236). The identity is
ββ'(145)(146) − αα'(235)(236) = (αβ−α'β')[(P'−Q')(G−P) − (P−Q)(G'−P')],
with P=α+1/α, Q=β+1/β, G=γ+1/γ and primes likewise. It checks numerically, e.g. α=2, α'=3, β=1, β'=2, γ=γ'=1 gives −1 = −1. It only involves rows 0,1,2, and expresses a product of minors through the symmetric quantities u+1/u appearing in (4)–(6).

PURPOSE. In the bundle 'AbelTheta' this is presumably auxiliary algebra for a configuration of six quantities with an involution u→1/u (possibly linked to genus-2 / theta-characteristic relations). The page itself contains only the linear-algebra elimination. The precise intended application is unsure.
errors: The middle expression of the first ratio line is not a typo: it is the same ratio computed from rows (0,1,3). Its equality with the (0,1,2) version needs the linear dependence (2), as Riemann notes ('und (2)'). It is not an identity in general.
All steps tacitly assume λ''≠0, λλ'≠0 and non-vanishing denominators (generic position). This is not stated.

The leading factor in the last line, transcribed 'ββ'γ', must be ββ'. The identity is invariant under γ→1/γ (which swaps (145)↔(146) and (235)↔(236) and fixes γ+1/γ), so an extra γ would break it. It is probably a misread bracket. With ββ' the identity checks numerically.
The two scribbled expansion lines (−αα'+αβ'−β'/γ−α'/γ, …) have sign slips relative to (136): it should be +α'/γ, and in the second line −α'β, +β/γ'. They are scratch work only.
The written form (136)(236)/((254)(154)) differs from the directly derived (136)(263)/((154)(245)) by two column transpositions. The signs cancel, so it is correct.

results.what: Condition for four linear forms in six variables with coefficient pattern (u,1/u) to be linearly dependent; eliminating multipliers gives (3)–(6)
results.modern_name: rank condition / left-kernel elimination for a 4×6 matrix

results.what: Ratios of 3×3 minors are independent of the chosen row triple when the rows are dependent; mediant argument giving (136)/(154) = Aa/Cc = Bb/Dd
results.modern_name: proportionality of maximal minors (Plücker-type coordinates of a row space)

results.what: ββ'β''/(γγ'γ'') = (136)(263)/((154)(245)) and ββ'β''γγ'γ'' = (135)(235)/((264)(164)) under the dependence condition
results.modern_name: expressing parameters of a special linear configuration through Plücker coordinates

deep.surprise_reason: The page is careful but routine elimination and determinant manipulation for a special linear system with a u↔1/u symmetry. It is of interest only as dated (April 1858) scratch work in the Abel/theta bundle. No result here would be attributed to anyone later.

checkable.asserts: (3) follows from the two α-equations of (2) (should be 0)
Key step linking (6) to C·b (should be 0)
Quotient of the two first members equals ββ'β''/(γγ'γ'') (should be 0)
Last-line identity with leading factor ββ' (expected 0; verified numerically at α=2, α'=3, β=1, β'=2, γ=γ'=1)

transcription_corrections: '[-±-] (136)/(154)': the struck character before (136)/(154) is a cancelled scribble; the intended statement is simply '= (136)/(154)'.
'(αβγ')/(αγβ')' at the end of the first ratio line is most likely (α β 1/γ)/(α γ 1/β), i.e. column-notation for (136)/(154).
Last line: the leading factor is ββ', not ββ'γ. The brackets (α 1/β γ), (α 1/β 1/γ), (1/α β γ), (1/α β 1/γ) are 3×3 minors in column notation, i.e. (145), (146), (235), (236).
The line read 'ββ'β''γγ'γ'' = (135)(235)/((264)(164))' is consistent with the derivation (γ→1/γ applied to the previous line); the first symbol in the image looks garbled but should be β.
Scribbled lines: signs of some terms differ from the true expansion of (136); this is scratch work.
